projects.name: and3rn3t
projects.description: The site you're on: plain ES modules on GitHub Pages, pages pre-rendered from JSON, a WebAssembly particle hero, and a Cloudflare Worker for the live parts.
projects.longDescription: This portfolio is plain ES modules served straight from GitHub Pages, with no framework and no build step. The project and post pages are generated from JSON data files, so they read fine without JavaScript, and the home page runs a short critical path before starting each feature as it nears the viewport. The hero background is a particle flow-field written in AssemblyScript and compiled to WebAssembly, falling back to a WebGL gradient and then to CSS. A Cloudflare Worker on the same domain handles what static hosting can't: view counts, a Turnstile-protected guestbook, recent GitHub activity, a public status page fed by its own uptime probe, and a read-only MCP server so AI agents can query the portfolio. A daily GitHub Actions workflow refreshes the GitHub data and regenerates the pages.
highlights: Framework-free ES modules; project and post pages pre-rendered from JSON
AssemblyScript → WebAssembly particle flow-field with WebGL and CSS fallbacks
Cloudflare Worker for view counts, the guestbook, live activity and the /status/ page
Agent-ready: llms.txt, Markdown responses and a read-only MCP server
Vitest, Playwright + axe and Lighthouse CI budgets (desktop and mobile) on every change

projects.name: health

screenshot.alt: The gait analysis page of VitalSense: gait quality, average speed, cadence and balance score, with a choice of LiDAR or walking-pattern analysis.

projects.description: Apple Health insights, fall-risk scoring and caregiver alerts: a native iOS app feeding a web dashboard on Cloudflare Workers.
projects.longDescription: VitalSense turns Apple Health data into something a family can act on. A native SwiftUI app reads HealthKit and scores gait, balance and mobility for fall risk (using the iPhone's LiDAR sensor or its motion sensors), and when it detects a fall it alerts the people who look after you. The web side is a React 19 dashboard backed by Cloudflare Workers (Hono), with Durable Objects streaming live data between the phone and the browser over WebSockets, and a caregiver view for remote monitoring. It's live at health.andernet.dev.
highlights: Live at health.andernet.dev
Fall-risk scoring from gait, balance and mobility, with fall detection and caregiver alerts
Gait analysis from iPhone LiDAR depth sensing or the motion sensors, no wearable needed
Native SwiftUI + HealthKit app, with CoreML on the device
Cloudflare Workers (Hono) and Durable Objects for real-time sync over WebSockets
Tested with Vitest, Playwright and XCTest

projects.name: homehub
projects.description: An iOS-inspired smart home dashboard: Philips Hue control, live Arlo camera streaming, scenes and automations. A React 19 PWA on Cloudflare.
projects.longDescription: HomeHub is the control panel for my house, designed to feel like a native iOS app. It drives Philips Hue lights (colour included), streams Arlo cameras with DASH/HLS playback, and runs time-, condition- and geofence-based automations, which can also be built visually in a drag-and-drop flow designer. It's a React 19 PWA on Cloudflare Pages with Workers and KV behind it, and it keeps working offline from a local cache with optimistic updates.
highlights: Philips Hue control with colour, and live Arlo camera streaming (DASH/HLS)
Automations with time, condition and geofence triggers, plus a drag-and-drop flow designer
Offline-first PWA: local cache, optimistic updates and a precaching service worker
Edge back end on Cloudflare Workers and KV

projects.name: weather
projects.description: A React and TypeScript weather web app with an iOS-style interface, Capacitor for mobile, deployed on Cloudflare.
projects.longDescription: The web predecessor to my native weather app: a React and TypeScript weather app with an iOS-style interface, built mobile-first, with Capacitor for native mobile features. It's still deployed at weather.andernet.dev. The repository is archived.
highlights: iOS-style interface, built mobile-first
Capacitor for native mobile features
Deployed on Cloudflare at weather.andernet.dev

projects.name: couple-connect
projects.description: A relationship app for couples: shared daily challenges, progress tracking and rewards. React 19 on Cloudflare Pages.
projects.longDescription: An app to help couples build habits together, by turning relationship activities into small challenges. Each partner has a profile, there are daily challenges, progress tracking and rewards for milestones, and it's designed mobile-first. Built with React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Radix UI, deployed to Cloudflare Pages. The repository is archived.
highlights: Partner profiles, daily challenges and progress tracking
Rewards for milestones
Mobile-first design

projects.name: network
projects.description: A Python client for the UniFi Network controller API, with automated data collection, analytics and alerting.
projects.longDescription: A Python library and collector for a local UniFi controller, tested against a UDM Pro. It polls devices and clients on a schedule into SQLite, scores network health, and raises rule-based alerts with notifications. A collection cycle of 6 devices and 38+ clients takes about three seconds. The repository is archived.
highlights: Local UniFi controller client, tested on a UDM Pro
Scheduled collection into SQLite, about three seconds per cycle
Health scoring and rule-based alerts

projects.name: net-traffic
projects.description: A home network traffic dashboard: packet capture on a Raspberry Pi 5, with the dashboard served from Cloudflare Pages.
projects.longDescription: NetInsight splits network monitoring in two. A Raspberry Pi 5 on the home network does the packet capture and storage and serves an API; the dashboard is a TypeScript front end on Cloudflare Pages that reaches the Pi through a tunnel. It shows traffic in real time, breaks it down by protocol, maps where connections go, and flags anomalies.
highlights: Packet capture, storage and API on a Raspberry Pi 5
Dashboard on Cloudflare Pages, connected to the Pi through a tunnel
Real-time traffic, protocol breakdown and geographic distribution
Anomaly detection

projects.name: huggingface
projects.description: Browse Hugging Face datasets and models, compare them, and try the Inference API, in one interface.
projects.longDescription: A learning tool for the Hugging Face ecosystem. It has a dataset browser with filters by task, language and size; a model explorer with model cards and code snippets; an API playground that sends requests to the Inference API and shows formatted responses; and a side-by-side model comparison. Built with React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. The repository is archived.
highlights: Dataset browser and model explorer
Inference API playground with code examples
Side-by-side model comparison

projects.name: hack
projects.description: A horror-themed hacking simulator and capture-the-flag game in Rust, with 26+ challenges for beginners and up.
projects.longDescription: A terminal hacking game with a horror story wrapped around it. There are 26+ capture-the-flag challenges, from Base64 and Caesar ciphers through file-system exploration, network analysis and SQL injection to reverse engineering, with hints aimed at people who aren't security folks yet, and a sanity meter that drops as you go deeper. It's written in Rust, with difficulty variants, a practice mode that generates challenges, and several save slots. The repository is archived.
highlights: 26+ CTF challenges, from encodings to SQL injection and reverse engineering
Beginner-friendly hints, with a horror story and a sanity meter
Difficulty variants and a practice mode with generated challenges
Written in Rust

projects.name: dbt
projects.description: A data science workspace: Python analysis, dbt transformations and Jupyter notebooks.
projects.longDescription: A workspace for practising analytics engineering end to end. Python scripts fetch public data (including data.gov) into a raw, staging and processed layout, a dbt project models it in SQL, and Jupyter notebooks are where the exploring happens. It runs in Docker with a local database, and pytest covers the scripts.
highlights: Python fetchers for public data sources, including data.gov
dbt project for SQL transformations on top of the raw data
Jupyter notebooks for exploration
Docker setup with a local database; pytest for the scripts

projects.name: minecraft
projects.description: A Minecraft server stack for the Raspberry Pi 5: Docker deployment, automated and offsite backups, a Flask REST API and a React admin panel.
projects.longDescription: The interesting part isn't Minecraft, it's the operations around it. The stack is tuned for the Pi 5 (ARM64): Docker Compose with systemd units, scheduled backups with retention plus offsite copies to R2, S3 or B2, multi-world management, and plugin and mod management across Vanilla, Paper, Spigot and Fabric. A Flask REST API and a React 19 admin panel (with roles, API keys and OAuth) manage it, and the Pi pulls the newest green commit on main every five minutes. On top sits a layer of family gameplay features, from graves and lucky blocks to a bedtime and a Claude-powered chat companion, driven by an event bus that reads the server log.
highlights: Docker Compose on a Raspberry Pi 5, started at boot by systemd
Scheduled backups with retention, plus offsite copies to R2, S3 or B2
Flask REST API and React admin panel with roles, API keys and OAuth
Auto-deploys the newest green commit on main every five minutes
Family gameplay features on an event bus that reads the server log

projects.name: catastrophe
projects.description: CATastrophe: A Mischief Simulator. A 3D Unreal Engine 5 game where you play a cat causing havoc in a house without getting caught.
projects.longDescription: An experiment in Unreal Engine 5 and C++. You play a cat loose in a house: knock vases off shelves, scratch furniture, shred curtains and steal food for points, while people with vision cones patrol the rooms and catch you if they see you misbehaving. It's where I'm learning third-person character control, physics-driven interactions and stealth AI.
highlights: Third-person cat with sprint, jump and climb
Physics-driven objects, each worth points when knocked over or stolen
NPCs with vision cones and patrol routes
Gameplay written in C++ on Unreal Engine 5

projects.name: apple-music-dj
projects.description: An AI Apple Music curator: it profiles your real listening history and builds playlists in your library. An Agent Skill for Claude Code and OpenClaw.
projects.longDescription: Apple Music DJ is an Agent Skill: you talk to Claude Code or OpenClaw, and it reads your listening history through Apple's MusicKit API (recently played, heavy rotation, library, ratings and Replay) to build a profile of your taste. From that it makes playlists straight into your Apple Music library with nine strategies, from deep cuts and decade throwbacks to songs-like-X and two-person blends, sequenced to build and wind down rather than shuffled. Nothing in your account changes until you approve it, and a built-in demo with a fictional listener lets anyone try it without an Apple Developer account. The core needs only Python 3.11, with no pip packages. It's published on ClawHub.
highlights: Taste profiling from your real listening history through MusicKit
Nine playlist strategies, sequenced with an energy arc
Read-only until you approve a change
No-account demo mode against a fictional listener
Published on ClawHub; works in Claude Code and OpenClaw

projects.name: guess

screenshot.alt: The Andernator start screen: a character-guessing game with three detective personalities and a daily challenge.

projects.description: An Akinator-style guessing game that shows its reasoning: Bayesian scoring over 53,000+ characters, with every question explained.
projects.longDescription: Think of a character and Andernator asks yes/no questions until it guesses. Unlike Akinator, it shows its work: each question is picked for information gain, every answer updates Bayesian probabilities over 53,000+ characters with 224 attributes each, and the UI explains why it asked what it asked. When it guesses wrong you can teach it the character. There's a daily challenge, three difficulty levels, category filters and a Wordle-style share card. The front end is React 19 on Cloudflare Pages; the engine runs on Workers against D1, and GPT-4o (through Cloudflare AI Gateway) reads free-text answers. It's live at andernator.com.
highlights: Live at andernator.com, playable in any browser
Bayesian scoring with information-gain question selection, explained as you play
53,000+ characters with 224 attributes each, in Cloudflare D1
Teaching mode, a daily challenge and a Wordle-style share card

projects.name: weather-app
projects.description: A SwiftUI weather app for iOS 26 with Liquid Glass design, widgets and Live Activities, plus an Android companion in Jetpack Compose.
projects.longDescription: A native weather app built to keep up with Apple's platform as iOS 26 arrived. Forecasts come from Open-Meteo, US severe-weather alerts from the National Weather Service, and radar from RainViewer. It has hourly and 14-day forecasts, air quality and UV, Swift Charts graphs, favourites saved with SwiftData, home- and lock-screen widgets, Live Activities and Siri shortcuts, all in the Liquid Glass design. The architecture is MVVM with @Observable and async/await, and there's an Android companion written in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose.
highlights: Liquid Glass design for iOS 26
Open-Meteo forecasts, NWS severe-weather alerts and RainViewer radar
Widgets, Live Activities and Siri shortcuts
Favourites in SwiftData; MVVM with @Observable and async/await
Android companion in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose

projects.name: remote
projects.description: A SwiftUI remote for Denon AV receivers, built to iOS 26 design guidelines: Liquid Glass, multi-zone control and Dynamic Island now-playing.
projects.longDescription: A native iOS app for Denon AV receivers that finds them on the local network with Bonjour and controls them directly. It covers power, volume (with a configurable safety limit), 13 inputs, 18 surround modes, tone and Dynamic EQ, a sleep timer, saved scenes, and independent control of Zones 2 and 3, with now-playing in the Dynamic Island. It's also my testbed for the iOS 26 design language: Liquid Glass controls, the customisable toolbar API, split view on iPad and haptics throughout.
highlights: Finds receivers on the local network with Bonjour
Power, volume, 13 inputs and 18 surround modes, plus Zones 2 and 3
Now-playing in the Dynamic Island
Liquid Glass UI, customisable toolbar, iPad split view and keyboard shortcuts

projects.name: fastlane
projects.description: A single-player life-sim board game where the rat race is the board: 60 hours a week to reach four life goals before your rival does.
projects.longDescription: You get 60 hours a week. Rent is due, the fridge is empty, your clothes are wearing out, and your rival Riley is already at work. Travel a twelve-stop city loop, take jobs, earn degrees and buy the things that make life bearable, and hit your wealth, happiness, education and career goals before Riley does. Riley plays by exactly the same rules: its AI calls the same engine actions the buttons do. Classic life-sim mechanics (weekly rent and eviction, a drifting economy, a lottery, street robbery) are kept, and the busywork is modernised away. Built with React, TypeScript and Vite, with the engine and UI tested in Vitest.
highlights: Four goals (wealth, happiness, education, career) with adjustable targets
A rival AI that uses the same engine actions as the player
Twelve-stop city loop with jobs, school, rent, shopping and random events
Engine and UI tested with Vitest
